name: Trowelled (steel-trowel closed finish)
process: The setting coat of lime and fine sand or marble dust is laid in two or three thin coats in quick succession, lightly wetted and floated with a timber float as it begins to set, then polished with a steel trowel as it hardens. Over the following hours and days the plasterer wets, scours and polishes again to close shrinkage cracks and crazing. A trowel gives a fine closed finish; wooden and sponge floats alone give an open, sandy texture.

steps.source: Napier, W. & Jenkins, M. (2018) Inform Guide: Plain Lime Plastering. Historic Environment Scotland, https://www.historicenvironment.scot/archives-and-research/publications/publication/?publicationId=67d4d72c-7b8c-4622-a244-a94b01090177

steps.step: float with a timber float as it begins to set
polish with a steel trowel as it sets to a hardened finish
re-wet, scour and polish over hours and days to control shrinkage cracking and crazing

layers.source: Ratcliffe, T. (2006) Internal Lime-Plastering. The Building Conservation Directory, https://www.buildingconservation.com/articles/internallimeplast/lime_plaster.htm ('two or three very thin layers', laid in alternate directions)

closedVersusOpen.text: a trowel achieves a fine closed finish; a combination of wooden and sponge floats creates an open textured finish

classicalPolish.text: well-made stucco, laid thick in three sand and three marble-dust coats, takes a high polish like a thick silver mirror, while thin plaster cracks and soon decays
classicalPolish.source: Vitruvius, De Architectura VII.3.6 and VII.3.9, trans. J. Gwilt (1826), https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Vitruvius/7*.html

gaugedSetting.text: the setting coat mix can be gauged with plaster of Paris to minimise the need for scouring

surface.skin: Closed and dense: trowelling presses the fine calcite and binder to the face, so the finish is smoother and less porous at the surface than the body below.
surface.sheen: A soft sheen from the steel polish, strongest where the trowel pressed hardest; not a varnish gloss.
surface.texture: Long shallow arcs and overlaps of the trowel, laid in alternate directions coat by coat; broad, low clouding where suction varied.
surface.arrises: Formed against rules or run members; finished by hand, so slightly softened.
surface.evidence: C:/Users/anan9/Desktop/Projects/Musee Vision/windows/SourceArt/PBR/P1 (ambientCG Plaster001, CC0 1.0): trowel strokes in the normal map, clouding in the colour map.

photograph: Raking light shows long trowel arcs and slight undulation over metres; frontal light shows almost nothing but a faint sheen.
A specular highlight that is broad and soft, never a sharp reflection, except on a burnished stucco lustro finish.

unverified.reason: No measured BRDF or gloss reading of trowelled lime plaster was found. Needs a goniometric measurement or a tier (b) specimen under raking light.
No measured profile of trowel marks was found; the P1 evidence set shows their pattern but its height map is not calibrated.
